properties.biography: Telefon Tel Aviv was formed in the late 1990s in the United States by Joshua Eustis and Charles Cooper. They quickly gained recognition for their innovative approach to electronic music, combining IDM and ambient influences with glitchy textures and downtempo rhythms. Their debut album, "Fahrenheit Fair Enough," released in 2001, was critically acclaimed for its detailed production and emotional depth. The duo continued to evolve their sound with subsequent releases, notably "Map of What Is Effortless" in 2004. Tragically, Charles Cooper passed away in 2009, after which Joshua Eustis carried on the Telefon Tel Aviv name, releasing further albums and continuing to influence the electronic music scene.
properties.known_for: Known for their intricate electronic production, emotive soundscapes, and blending of organic and synthetic textures.
properties.description: Telefon Tel Aviv is an American electronic music duo originally consisting of Joshua Eustis and Charles Cooper. They are known for their complex, layered electronic compositions that blend elements of IDM, ambient, glitch, and downtempo music. Their sound is characterized by emotive melodies, intricate production techniques, and a fusion of organic and synthetic textures. After the tragic death of Charles Cooper in 2009, Joshua Eustis continued the project as a solo act, maintaining the signature style of Telefon Tel Aviv while exploring new sonic territories.
properties.cultural_impact: Telefon Tel Aviv has been influential in shaping the IDM and ambient electronic music scenes, inspiring a generation of producers with their emotive and intricate sound design. Their work is noted for bridging the gap between experimental electronic music and accessible melodic structures, impacting both underground and mainstream electronic music cultures.
properties.performance_style: Telefon Tel Aviv's live performances are immersive and atmospheric, often featuring complex electronic arrangements and a focus on creating an emotive experience for the audience.

properties.biography: Modeselektor was formed in Berlin, Germany, by Gernot Bronsert and Sebastian Szary. Both members had backgrounds in electronic music production and shared a passion for pushing the boundaries of techno and electronic music. They gained recognition in the early 2000s for their unique sound that combined glitchy textures, heavy basslines, and diverse rhythmic patterns. Over the years, they have released several albums and EPs, collaborated with artists like Apparat, and contributed significantly to the electronic music community through their label and live performances.
properties.known_for: Known for their eclectic and experimental approach to electronic and techno music, blending various styles and innovative production techniques.

Their music is characterized by its eclecticism, innovative production techniques, and energetic beats. properties.vocals: Primarily instrumental; when vocals appear they are typically sampled snippets, processed voices or sparse sung lines rather than a lead vocal approach. Hebden favors textural and chopped vocal treatments rather than conventional singing.
properties.biography: Kieran Hebden began making music in the 1990s as a member of the instrumental/post‑rock band Fridge before launching his solo project Four Tet in the late 1990s. Early Four Tet releases blended folky acoustic samples with electronic beats, winning attention from the IDM and indie scenes. Hebden released a string of influential albums—most notably Rounds (2003), There Is Love In You (2010) and New Energy (2017)—and worked in crossover settings with jazz drummer Steve Reid. He founded the independent Text Records imprint to release his own material and occasional edits and singles. Over two decades he has expanded his palette from intimate, sample‑based compositions to dancefloor edits and club‑focused productions while maintaining a reputation for meticulous arrangements and dynamic live sets.
properties.known_for: Blending electronic and acoustic sounds, intricate sample-based arrangements, dynamic live sets and influential genre-blurring productions; founder of Text Records.
properties.description: Four Tet is the solo project of British producer Kieran Hebden, who rose from the UK post‑rock scene into a leading figure in contemporary electronic music. He is known for combining samples, acoustic instrumentation and electronic production to create warm, rhythmic, and melodically rich tracks that move between ambient, IDM and dancefloor-oriented styles. Hebden has released critically acclaimed albums (including Rounds, There Is Love In You and New Energy), collaborated with jazz drummer Steve Reid, founded the independent label Text Records, and is celebrated for both his immersive live sets and DJ performances.
properties.cultural_impact: Four Tet helped popularize a melodic, sample‑based strain of electronic music that bridges IDM, folktronica and dance music. His releases and edits influenced a generation of producers and DJs, contributed to the crossover of experimental electronica into clubs, and established a DIY model via his Text Records imprint that encouraged genre‑fluid releases and direct engagement with underground and mainstream audiences.
properties.performance_style: A hybrid between DJ sets and live performance: Hebden uses laptops, samplers and live processing to loop, layer and rework material in real time, moving between delicate ambient passages and propulsive dancefloor sections. Sets often emphasize long transitions, subtle build-ups and rhythmic detail.

properties.biography: Born in St Albans in 1979, Christopher Stephen Clark began making music in his teens and experimented with building his own equipment. While a student he performed at a Warp Records party (December 2000) and soon signed to the label, releasing Clarence Park (2001) as Chris Clark. Over the 2000s he evolved from hard-edged electronic productions to records incorporating live instrumentation and folk-tinged touches (Body Riddle, Turning Dragon, Iradelphic). Clark has composed scores for dance, film and television (including The Last Panthers and Kiri), released work on Warp and Deutsche Grammophon and founded his own imprint, Throttle Records. His output blends meticulous IDM sound design with cinematic composition and occasional vocal processing.
properties.known_for: Detailed IDM sound design, textured electronic-to-orchestral hybrids, cinematic scores and releases on Warp/Deutsche Grammophon.
properties.description: Christopher Stephen Clark (born 29 August 1979) is a British electronic musician and composer whose work spans IDM, techno, ambient and electroacoustic music. A longtime Warp Records artist who also runs Throttle Records, Clark combines detailed sound design, processed acoustic elements and occasional vocals while composing albums, scores for film/TV and music for contemporary dance.
properties.cultural_impact: Clark helped expand the palette of early-2000s IDM by integrating live instrumentation, folk textures and cinematic composition into electronic production. As a Warp Records stalwart and composer for award-earning TV and dance projects, he has influenced contemporary electronic composers and reinforced IDM's crossover into film/TV scoring and modern classical contexts.
properties.performance_style: Live sets blend sequenced electronic material with live/processed instrumentation and vocals, often incorporating improvisation and multimedia or installation-based elements for a cinematic, immersive experience.
